streams.the_witness_problem_is_a_CLASS_and_I_am_:
`gh pr create` leaves NO local artefact proving a PR exists. `refs/pull/*` appear only after a fetch - the command does not write them - so the PR number and URL are MY report over the network and can never be the coordinator's measurement. Unlike the push, opening a PR has no witness of its own. I am stating that as a class rather than looking for a substitute, because he asked for exactly that and because a substitute would be worse than an absence.

BUT A WITNESS IS DERIVABLE, and his refinement of my proposal is the precise version. Measured: the remote PUBLISHES refs/pull/* - 79 of them exist there now - and such a ref exists only for an existing pull request. Its sha must equal e5132934, this slice's unique commit, pushed twenty minutes earlier. So after the fetch HE reads, himself and without network: a local ref exists, and its sha is that commit. His measurement is therefore 'a PR whose head is THIS commit exists'. The NUMBER and the URL stay my report. Two halves with two sources, and the report must not merge them into one voice - which is the form he used for stage 8 and the form this stage keeps.

THE LIMIT, carried in his words because a reader could take one for the other: the reflog of the fetched ref will read `fetch …: storing ref`, NOT `update by push`. That verb attributes the LOCAL ref to the fetch, which is correct and expected. What proves the PR exists is the sha plus the ref being published server-side - never the verb in that reflog.
streams.the_positive_control_CHANGED_SHAPE_becau:
His finding, and the general lesson is worth more than the stage. Stage 5's positive control was 'per-worktree FETCH_HEAD absent -> exists'. That stage SUCCEEDED, and in succeeding it SPENT its own control: the file now exists (verified: /home/linux/Developer/skipi-crewing/.git/worktrees/crewing-898-20261104/FETCH_HEAD, sha d735ef165a4a277ed96aef52a564dd9cb183648a3df7310b9664a8f8ace86866, mtime 1793808424.105761294, body `f145c601… branch 'main' of https://github.com/CaptTymur/skipi-crewing`). So this stage's fetch REWRITES it rather than creating it, and 'the file is there' would be true even if the fetch never ran.

A SUCCESSFUL ACTION CAN STRIP A PREDICATE OF ITS DISCRIMINATING POWER. That is the rule, and it is not about this file: any control built on a first-time transition is single-use, and the stage that uses it must hand its successor a different one. Here the control becomes CONTENT: the sha is pinned before and must DIFFER after, with the nanosecond mtime as the secondary reading. NOT existence, and NOT the inode - measured earlier in this task, git rewrites this file in place, so the inode is stable across fetches and ctime equals mtime to the nanosecond.
streams.a_negative_control_that_gh_did_NOT_push_: His, and it needed nothing new. `--head` is a promise from gh's own help - 'explicitly skip any forking or pushing behavior' - and a promise is not a measurement. It is CHECKED by three readings taken after the stage: refs/heads/feat/crewing-898-login-texts-20261104 and refs/remotes/origin/feat/crewing-898-login-texts-20261104 must still hold e5132934, and the remote-tracking reflog must still have EXACTLY ONE line. Any push by `gh` would add a second line, so stage 8's own artefact is the detector, already in place and currently measured at 1 line. A second reason not to let gh near a push: `gh auth status` reports `Git operations protocol: ssh` while this remote is HTTPS.
streams.dry_run_was_unavailable_so_the_rehearsal: Worth saying out loud rather than omitting. The ordinary way to rehearse an external command is `--dry-run`, and gh's help says it 'Print details instead of creating the PR. MAY STILL PUSH GIT CHANGES.' So it is not a dry run in the sense this protocol needs, and it is not used. The driver was rehearsed against a STUB `gh` plus a fixture remote carrying a synthetic refs/pull/<N>/head - the same technique as the stubbed guard in stages 6 and 7, and for the same reason: running the real instrument outside a window would BE the action.
streams.mutates_is_now_a_read_field_and_I_differ:
His new inspector check requires every `mutates` token to be covered by some `surfaces.*.writes` under `overlaps()`. The field was required by AGENTS prose and read by nothing until now, so a request could declare a shared object in `mutates`, duplicate it in `resource_identities`, and reserve NOTHING - because collisions are built from `surfaces` alone. None of my seven bundles carried `mutates` at all, so none was affected; this stage carries it.

WHERE I DIFFER, with the reason rather than silently: he suggested leaving the shared .git/config OUT, on the ground that I guard it rather than write it, and for the PUSH that was exactly right - stage 8 measured it byte-identical before and after. For THIS stage the actor is `gh`, not git-push, and writing `remote.origin.gh-resolved` on first use is documented gh behaviour that I cannot cheaply exclude: today that key is unset and there are zero `gh.*` keys. Three findings in a row on this very genus - the index in stage 3a, the per-worktree FETCH_HEAD in stage 5, the reflog in stage 8 - all were undeclared writes into a gitdir shared by 86 worktrees. So I would rather over-declare a shared file than risk a fourth, and it sits in both `writes` and `mutates` with the FINDING-on-change kept as detection. If he judges that too broad I will take it out, but the asymmetry of cost points this way.
